lines.en: Camila, you look exhausted. How long had you been hiking when you reached the ridge?
lines.pt: Camila, você parece exausto. Há quanto tempo você vinha caminhando quando chegou à crista da serra?

lines.en: We had been walking for almost five hours, and my boots had been hurting since the second hour.
lines.pt: Estávamos caminhando havia quase cinco horas, e minhas botas machucavam desde a segunda hora.

lines.en: Five hours! Had you been following the main trail the whole time?
lines.pt: Cinco horas! Vocês vinham seguindo a trilha principal o tempo todo?

lines.en: No, we had been following a shortcut that a local guy recommended, and it got steeper and steeper.
lines.pt: Não, vínhamos seguindo um atalho que um morador recomendou, e ele ficava cada vez mais íngreme.

lines.en: That explains the blisters. I had been waiting at the car park for ages, and I was worried.
lines.pt: Isso explica as bolhas. Eu estava esperando no estacionamento havia séculos, e fiquei preocupada.

lines.en: Sorry, Diego. My phone had been losing signal all morning, so I could not call you.
lines.pt: Desculpe, Diego. Meu celular perdia sinal desde cedo, então não consegui ligar para você.

lines.en: Had the weather been bad too? The sky had been getting darker since noon.
lines.pt: O tempo também estava ruim? O céu vinha escurecendo desde o meio-dia.

lines.en: Not really. The wind had been blowing hard on the ridge, but the views were worth it.
lines.pt: Nem tanto. O vento vinha soprando forte na crista, mas as vistas valeram a pena.

lines.en: How long had you been resting at the summit before you started back down?
lines.pt: Há quanto tempo vocês descansavam no topo antes de começarem a descer?

lines.en: Only twenty minutes. We had been drinking our last water, so we had to hurry before sunset.
lines.pt: Só vinte minutos. Estávamos bebendo nossa última água, então tivemos de correr antes do pôr do sol.

lines.en: Next time, let’s plan better. We had been talking about this hike for months, after all.
lines.pt: Da próxima vez, vamos planejar melhor. Afinal, falávamos dessa trilha havia meses.

facts.label: Past perfect contínuo
facts.sub: Duração antes de um momento passado: had been walking for hours. Pergunta: How long had you been walking? Negativa: hadn’t been.

facts.label: Havia + gerúndio
facts.sub: Use had been + verbo com -ing para falar de uma ação que já durava até outro momento do passado: We had been walking for hours when it started to rain. Ela explica causas e cansaço.

facts.label: Por e desde
facts.sub: Use for com um período (for five hours) e since com o ponto de partida (since noon). Em B2, você usa as duas formas para dar precisão: I had been waiting for an hour. He had been waiting since nine.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: Had been + -ing shows duration before a past moment.
We say “We had been walk for hours”.
For gives a period and since gives a starting point.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: Had been + -ing shows duration before a past moment. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
We say “We had been walk for hours”. → Falso (We say had been walking.)
For gives a period and since gives a starting point. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)

pages.title: The long way down · 1/3
paragraphs: It is late afternoon in a car park near the Blue Mountains, west of Sydney. Fern has been checking her watch for a long time. The sun is going down behind the trees. At last, her friend Dan walks out of the forest. His clothes are dusty, and he limps a little. Fern wants to hear the whole story of the day.

“Dan, you look exhausted. How long had you been hiking when you reached the ridge?” says Fern. “We had been walking for almost five hours, and my boots had been hurting since the second hour.” says Dan. “Five hours! Had you been following the main trail the whole time?” says Fern.

paragraphs: “Only twenty minutes. We had been drinking our last water, so we had to hurry before sunset.” says Dan. “Next time, let’s plan better. We had been talking about this hike for months, after all.” says Fern. Dan sits down on the bench and takes off his boots. Fern gives him a bottle of cold water. They laugh about the shortcut that was not short at all. The sky turns orange over the valley. Dan says it was the hardest walk of his life. They drive home and plan a shorter trip for next month.
